entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Temple of Bona Dea ('Good Goddess'), located on the Aventine Hill in Rome, was the principal sanctuary of Bona Dea — a Roman goddess of fertility, healing, and women, whose identity was kept deliberately mysterious and whose cult was one of the most strictly observed single-sex religious institutions in Rome, with her annual December festival (held in the house of the current consul or praetor) being one of the most closely guarded religious ceremonies of the Roman world, from which men were absolutely excluded.

Bona Dea's cult was remarkable in Roman religion for its strict sex exclusivity: her festival, held in December in the home of a high magistrate's wife, was presided over by the Vestal Virgins and attended only by women of rank. No man was permitted to know what transpired — her name, her image, and her rites were kept secret from men. This made her the center of Rome's most celebrated religious scandal: in 62 BCE, the populist politician Publius Clodius Pulcher disguised himself as a woman to infiltrate the festival held in Julius Caesar's house (presided over by Caesar's wife Pompeia). Caesar subsequently divorced Pompeia, giving the famous reason that 'Caesar's wife must be above suspicion' — a phrase that has passed into common use.

The Aventine Temple itself was the center of the public cult, where a sacred snake was kept and medical herbs were grown and distributed. The temple was associated with healing, and women (but not men) could visit to receive medicinal herbs. The Bona Dea cult represents one of Roman religion's most distinctive gendered religious spaces.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Temple of Bona Dea — center of Rome's most exclusively female religious cult, site of the Clodius scandal producing Caesar's famous 'wife above suspicion' divorce, and representing women's autonomous sacred space in Roman religion — is historically significant for both its gender dimensions and its connection to Republican Rome's most notable religious scandal.
